cards.text: The Lord GOD has been showing visions to Amos, a man from Tekoa who brings His word to Israel, and the last one ends with the Lord rising up against the house of Jeroboam (Amos 1:1; 7:9). Now Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sends word to Jeroboam king of Israel. And friend, this is NOT a thank-you note.

cards.question: In his message to King Jeroboam, what does Amaziah the priest accuse Amos of?

cards.text: "The land cannot bear all his words," Amaziah adds. The LAND, friend. Not just Amaziah. The whole COUNTRY needs to go lie down.

cards.question: Amaziah tells the king what Amos has been saying. How does Amos say Jeroboam will die?
Amaziah also reports that Amos said Israel will go into exile, away from their homeland.

cards.text: Then Amaziah turns to Amos himself: "Go away, you seer!" No hello. No asking about the trip. Just GO. GO. GO!

cards.question: Amaziah tells Amos to flee to the land of ___.

cards.text: Earn your bread there, Amaziah says, and do your prophesying there. But never prophesy at Bethel again.

cards.question: Amaziah says Amos can never prophesy at Bethel again. Why not?

cards.text: Now Amos answers. And he opens by telling Amaziah who he was before any of this.

cards.question: Amos tells Amaziah he was a prophet and the son of a prophet.
So what was Amos doing before he ever showed up at Bethel?

cards.text: Then Amos says the LORD took him from following the flock. Friend, I RELATE. One day you're a 25-cent stamper in the back of a junk drawer, under a pile of takeout menus. Next day you've got a gold base and a JOB.

cards.question: When the LORD took Amos from the flock, He told him, Go ___ to My people Israel.

cards.text: Then Amos turns it all the way around: "Now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD." Friend, the man who just got told to leave is about to do the talking.

cards.question: When Amos says to hear the word of the LORD, that word is for King Jeroboam.

cards.text: Then Amos says, "Therefore this is what the LORD says:" Amaziah's wife will become a prostitute in the city, and his sons and daughters will fall by the sword.

cards.question: The LORD says Amaziah's land will be ___ by a measuring line.
The LORD says Amaziah himself will die on pagan soil.

cards.text: Then the word closes with that line again: "Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland." Amaziah told Amos never to prophesy at Bethel again. Friend, the herdsman just delivered the LORD's word right there at Bethel.

findings.problem: The fact that the Lord GOD has been showing Amos visions is cited as Amos 1:1; 7:9. The visions themselves are in Amos 7:1-9 ("This is what the Lord GOD showed me," 7:1, 7:4, 7:7). Amos 1:1 only says what Amos saw concerning Israel, and 7:9 is only the end of the last vision. The reference for the visions should be Amos 7:1-9, with Amos 1:1 kept for Tekoa.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the quote, "The LAND, friend.", "Not just Amaziah." and "The whole COUNTRY needs to go lie down." It needs to come down to 1 or 2 sentences, keeping the joke.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: The question asks "How does Amos say Jeroboam will die?" That states as fact that Amos said Jeroboam himself will die. The text gives this only as Amaziah's report (7:11). Amos's own words in 7:9 were against "the house of Jeroboam." Ask it as Amaziah's claim, for example "According to Amaziah, how did Amos say Jeroboam will die?"

rule.text: **Retelling:** Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the quote line, "No hello.", "No asking about the trip." and "Just GO. GO. GO!" It needs to come down to 1 or 2 sentences.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: The card is a flat paraphrase of 7:12-13 with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a summary, not the storyteller.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer says "fig trees," but the text says "sycamore-fig trees" (7:14). Use the text's name, for example "Herding and tending sycamore-figs."

rule.text: **Call things what the text calls them.**

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences. It needs to come down to 1 or 2.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: "Next day you've got a gold base" changes the backstory. In his backstory, the angel came at night and "In the blink of an eye" Papa Dorin was on his gold base. There was no next day.

rule.text: **His own world isn't Bible fact.** His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Amos 7:16 is never told. In that verse, Amos quotes Amaziah's own command back to him ("Do not prophesy against Israel; do not preach against the house of Isaac"), and 7:17's "Therefore" rests on it. Without it, the baker misses why the judgment falls on Amaziah. A story card should tell it, or a choice card should ask about it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote line, the Amaziah sentence and the "Friend, the herdsman" sentence. It needs to come down to 1 or 2.
